Redesign internal mechanisms

Previously HANS strictly followed pipe pulling paradigm. Signal
processing and effect-chain configuration happened right after an
incoming MIDI trigger. As a consequence, scalability was very
limited. The new design improves the scalability by pushing periodic
signal processing results and effect-chain configuration regardless of
the frequency of incoming MIDI triggers.

Implement midi input blocking

Processing all incoming midi note-on can lead to large CPU
loads. Time-based filtering of incoming midi events is one way to
avoid that.

Improve Seedgen's performance

Use less resource intensive algorithm for random number generation.

Simple benchmark results:

Old implementation:
>>> timeit.timeit('random.randrange(1, 102334156)', setup='import random', number=1000)
0.001168966293334961

New implementation:
>>> timeit.timeit('int(random.random()*13579)', setup='import random', number=1000)
0.0002548694610595703

Redesign effect-chain

The existing effect-chain implementation was not effective. Many xruns
occurred due to the on-the-fly object allocation.

The frequency shifter effect was dropped, frequency modulation is done
by changing sample playback speed.
